about: ORI's own paraphrases of the effect of each Chapter 3 rule unit (2021 VRC = 2021 IRC as amended by 13VAC5-63-210). These are summaries in ORI's words, not code text and not interpretations; read the linked official source. Bare numeric thresholds are kept where a rule needs them. Titles live in build_units.py (UNITS) and are ORI descriptions, not ICC section headings. Policy: docs/CITATION-POLICY.md.
license: CC0-1.0 (ORI text only; no ICC text is included)

paraphrases.R301.1: The house must be built to carry every load type through an unbroken path down to the foundation; following the prescriptive provisions counts as meeting this, and engineered parts must tie into that path.
paraphrases.R301.1.3: Where a building or element falls outside the prescriptive limits, that part must be designed by engineering methods, and the engineered part has to work with the rest of the conventionally framed house.
paraphrases.R301.2: Design follows the climatic and geographic criteria the locality records in its Table R301.2 (for example wind, snow, frost depth, termite and flood data).
paraphrases.R301.2.1: Structures and exterior components are designed for the mapped ultimate wind speed; above the prescriptive wind limits, engineered wind design is needed. Virginia adds wording on special wind regions.
paraphrases.R301.2.1.4: The designer assigns the site's wind exposure (surface roughness and terrain around the building) for each direction, which then drives wind pressures.
paraphrases.R301.2.2: The site's seismic design category decides which seismic provisions and limits apply; higher categories restrict the prescriptive method.
paraphrases.R301.2.3: Roofs are designed for the ground snow load recorded for the locality; above the prescriptive snow limit, engineered design is required.
paraphrases.R301.2.4: A house in a mapped flood hazard area must follow the flood-resistant construction section (R322).
paraphrases.R301.3: Each story's height is capped for prescriptive framing (wood, steel, masonry, concrete each have limits); taller stories need engineering or the listed exceptions.
paraphrases.R301.4: Design accounts for the actual weight of the construction and fixed equipment.
paraphrases.R301.5: Floors, decks, balconies, stairs, guards and handrails are designed for at least the tabulated live loads for their use (Table R301.5).
paraphrases.R301.6: Roofs are designed for at least the tabulated roof live load, based on roof slope and tributary area.
paraphrases.R301.7: Structural members may not deflect more than the tabulated span ratios for their use and finish (Table R301.7).
paraphrases.R301.8: Lumber and other member sizes in the code are nominal sizes unless the code says otherwise.
paraphrases.R302.1: Exterior walls closer to the lot line than the tabulated fire separation distance need a fire-resistance rating, and openings and penetrations in them are limited. Virginia adds exceptions for decks and open porches and for lots where setbacks keep walls at least 10 ft apart.
paraphrases.R302.1|Table R302.1(1) Projections row: Roof overhangs and other projections have minimum distances from the lot line and need fire protection within a band; Virginia changes the projections row of the table.
paraphrases.R302.2: Townhouse units need rated separation walls or paired rated walls between them (townhouses are outside ORI single-family scope).
paraphrases.R302.2.6: Each townhouse unit must be structurally independent, with listed exceptions; Virginia adds an exception for sprinkler penetrations (outside single-family scope).
paraphrases.R302.3: The two units of a duplex need rated wall and floor separation; Virginia changes this and adds an accessory-dwelling exception (outside ORI scope).
paraphrases.R302.4: Pipes, ducts and other penetrations through rated unit separations must be protected to keep the rating (outside single-family scope).
paraphrases.R302.5.1: A door from the garage into the house must meet the door type or rating the code lists; Virginia changes the door options.
paraphrases.R302.5.2: Ducts in the garage that pierce the garage-house separation must be of the specified steel gauge and may not open into the garage.
paraphrases.R302.5.3: Other penetrations through the garage-house separation must be filled or protected with an acceptable material (by reference to the fireblocking provisions).
paraphrases.R302.6: The garage must be separated from the house and attic by gypsum board of the tabulated type and thickness (Table R302.6), including supporting structure where applicable.
paraphrases.R302.7: Where the space under a stair is enclosed and accessible, its walls, underside and soffits need a gypsum board layer on the space side.
paraphrases.R302.8: Foam plastic use is governed by R316.
paraphrases.R302.9: Wall and ceiling finishes must not exceed the stated flame spread and smoke-developed indexes when tested to the named standard.
paraphrases.R302.10: Insulation, facings and vapor retarders must meet the stated flame spread and smoke-developed limits, with separate rules for loose-fill and exposed attic insulation.
paraphrases.R302.11: Concealed spaces that could let fire travel between stories or across long runs must be cut off with approved fireblocking materials at the listed locations.
paraphrases.R302.12: Where there is usable space above and below a floor-ceiling assembly, the concealed space must be divided so no compartment exceeds the area limit.
paraphrases.R302.13: The IRC requires a membrane on the underside of certain floor framing; Virginia deletes this section, so it does not apply.
paraphrases.R302.14: Combustible insulation must keep the stated clearance from recessed lights, fan motors and other devices that give off heat, unless the device is listed for contact.
paraphrases.R303.1: Habitable rooms need glazing and openable area of at least set percentages of floor area, unless mechanical ventilation and artificial light are provided.
paraphrases.R303.2: A room may count an adjoining room toward light and ventilation if the opening between them is large enough.
paraphrases.R303.3: Bathrooms and toilet rooms need an openable window of minimum size, or a mechanical exhaust to the outdoors.
paraphrases.R303.4: Tighter houses (below the air-leakage threshold) need a whole-house mechanical ventilation system.
paraphrases.R303.5: Outdoor air intakes must be kept the stated distances from exhausts, vents, streets and other contaminant sources.
paraphrases.R303.6: Outdoor air intake and exhaust openings need corrosion-resistant screens or louvers within the stated opening size range.
paraphrases.R303.7: Interior stairs need artificial lighting to a minimum level at treads and landings, with switching at each floor level for longer runs.
paraphrases.R303.8: Exterior stairs need a light source at or near the top landing, and basement exterior stairs need light at the bottom landing.
paraphrases.R303.9: Required windows must open onto a yard, court or public way meeting the stated minimum dimensions.
paraphrases.R303.10: Where winter design temperature is below the threshold, habitable rooms need heating able to hold the stated indoor temperature; Virginia adds an exception.
paraphrases.R303.10.1: Virginia adds R303.10.1: a dwelling rented with heat included must have heating meeting R303.10 during the heating season (October 15 to May 1).
paraphrases.R303.11: Virginia adds R303.11: outside openings needed for ventilation need tight insect screens of at least 16 mesh per inch, and insect screen doors need a self-closer.
paraphrases.R304.1: Every habitable room except a kitchen must have at least the minimum floor area.
paraphrases.R304.2: Habitable rooms other than kitchens must be at least the minimum dimension in every horizontal direction.
paraphrases.R304.3: Floor area under a ceiling lower than the stated height does not count toward the room's minimum area.
paraphrases.R305.1|habitable: Habitable spaces, hallways, and basement areas holding them need at least the minimum clear ceiling height; reviewers handle the sloped-ceiling and beam exceptions.
paraphrases.R305.1|bath-toilet-laundry: Bath, toilet and laundry rooms are allowed a lower minimum ceiling height than habitable rooms.
paraphrases.R305.1|Exception 1 sloped ceilings: Rooms with sloped ceilings may have part of the area below the minimum height, as long as a set share of the floor area meets it and low areas are excluded.
paraphrases.R305.1|Exception 2 fixtures and showers: Above bathroom fixtures and at the showerhead, only a stated clear height and area in front of the fixture is needed.
paraphrases.R305.1|Exception 3 beams and obstruction: Beams, girders, ducts and similar items may project below the minimum ceiling height by a stated amount.
paraphrases.R305.1.1: Basement parts without habitable space may have a lower ceiling, with further allowance under beams and ducts.
paraphrases.R306.1: Each dwelling needs at least a toilet (water closet), a lavatory, and either a tub or a shower.
paraphrases.R306.2: Each dwelling needs a kitchen area with a sink.
paraphrases.R306.3: Plumbing fixtures must drain to a public sewer or an approved private sewage system.
paraphrases.R306.4: Kitchen sinks, lavatories, tubs, showers and laundry fixtures must be supplied with hot and cold water.
paraphrases.R306.5: Virginia adds R306.5: plumbing must connect to a water source and a sewer (either may be public or private), and private wells and septic systems fall under the health authorities as USBC Part I section 103.5 provides.
paraphrases.R307.1: Fixtures need the minimum clearances in front and to the sides shown in the code figure.
paraphrases.R307.2: Walls around tubs with showers and around showers must have a smooth, nonabsorbent surface to the stated height.
paraphrases.R308.1: Each pane of safety glazing in a hazardous location needs a permanent identifying label, with a certificate option for some glazing.
paraphrases.R308.2: Louvered or jalousie glass must meet limits on thickness, blade length and edge treatment.
paraphrases.R308.3: Safety glazing must pass the named impact test standard at the category required for its location.
paraphrases.R308.4.1: Glazing in swinging, sliding and bifold doors is a hazardous location and needs safety glazing, with listed exceptions.
paraphrases.R308.4.2: Glazing within a set distance of a door edge and below a set height is a hazardous location, with listed exceptions.
paraphrases.R308.4.3: A window pane that is large, low to the floor, high at the top and near a walking surface (all conditions together) needs safety glazing.
paraphrases.R308.4.4: Glazing in guards and railings needs safety glazing regardless of size or height.
paraphrases.R308.4.5: Glazing in walls around tubs, showers, pools and hot tubs within a set height above the standing surface needs safety glazing; Virginia changes the height value to 60 in.
paraphrases.R308.4.6: Glazing near stairways, landings and ramps within the stated height and distance needs safety glazing unless a guard protects it.
paraphrases.R308.4.7: Glazing near the bottom tread of a stair, within stated height and horizontal limits, needs safety glazing unless protected.
paraphrases.R308.5: Windows built on site must be designed to the referenced IBC glass provisions.
paraphrases.R308.6: Skylights and sloped glazing need the listed glass types and, in some cases, screens below them; unit skylights must be tested and labeled.
paraphrases.R309.1: Garage floors must be noncombustible and slope so liquids drain toward a drain or the vehicle entrance.
paraphrases.R309.2: A carport must be open on at least the stated number of sides, and its floor must be noncombustible, or it is treated as a garage.
paraphrases.R309.3: Garages in flood hazard areas must follow the flood provisions for materials and openings.
paraphrases.R309.4: Automatic garage door openers must be listed and labeled to the named safety standard.
paraphrases.R309.5: Where sprinklers are installed in a garage, they must meet the stated design and coverage rules.
paraphrases.R310.1: Each sleeping room, basement and habitable attic needs an opening for escape and rescue. Its exit leads to a public route, or to an outdoor yard or court meeting the width requirement; Virginia revises this rule.
paraphrases.R310.1|yard or court width: An escape opening must open onto a street or other public way, or onto a yard or court at least the stated width (Virginia value 36 in).
paraphrases.R310.2.1|net clear area: The clear opening available through normal operation must reach the minimum area; openings at grade floor or below grade may be smaller.
paraphrases.R310.2.1|net clear height: The clear opening height in normal operation must be at least the minimum.
paraphrases.R310.2.1|net clear width: The clear opening width in normal operation must be at least the minimum.
paraphrases.R310.2.2: In the IRC this section holds the minimum escape-opening height and width; Virginia deletes it and moves the values into R310.2.1.
paraphrases.R310.2.3: The lowest point of the clear opening may be no higher than the maximum above the floor.
paraphrases.R310.2.4: An escape opening under a deck, porch or cantilever needs a clear path of set height to a yard or court.
paraphrases.R310.2.5: Escape openings must open from inside with no key, tool or special knowledge; any opening control device must meet the named standard.
paraphrases.R310.3: A side-hinged or sliding door can serve as the escape opening if it meets the stated conditions and leads outside.
paraphrases.R310.4.1: The area well at a below-grade escape opening must meet a minimum area and projection and allow the window to open fully.
paraphrases.R310.4.2: An area well deeper than the stated depth needs a permanent ladder or steps that do not block the window.
paraphrases.R310.4.3: Area wells must drain to the foundation drainage system, except where soil conditions allow otherwise.
paraphrases.R310.4.4: Covers, bars or grates over area wells must be removable from inside without keys or tools and with normal force.
paraphrases.R310.5: A replacement window in an escape opening may keep an existing smaller size if it is the manufacturer's largest fit and meets stated conditions.
paraphrases.R310.6: A dwelling addition with a sleeping room or basement triggers escape openings for the new space, with stated exceptions.
paraphrases.R310.7: Altering or repairing an existing basement triggers an escape opening only where new sleeping rooms or habitable space are created, subject to stated conditions.
paraphrases.R311.1: Each dwelling needs an exit path that runs from all parts of the house to the outside without passing through a garage; Virginia rewords this section.
paraphrases.R311.2: At least one side-hinged exterior exit door of minimum clear size is required, openable from inside without a key.
paraphrases.R311.3: Every exterior door needs a landing or floor on both sides, at least as wide as the door and of minimum depth, with a maximum slope.
paraphrases.R311.3.1: At the required exit door, the landing may be only a small step below the threshold; Virginia adds an exception using 8-1/4 in.
paraphrases.R311.3.2: At other exterior doors, the landing may be lower than the threshold by up to a set step (Virginia value 8-1/4 in).
paraphrases.R311.3.3: Storm and screen doors may open out over the exterior landing or stairs.
paraphrases.R311.4: Egress from habitable levels that are not at grade (including habitable attics and basements) must be by a ramp or stairway.
paraphrases.R311.5: Exterior landings, decks, balconies and stairs must be anchored to the structure or built to stand on their own, to resist vertical and lateral loads.
paraphrases.R311.6: Hallways must be at least the minimum width.
paraphrases.R311.7.1: Stairs must be at least the minimum clear width above handrail height and below the headroom limit, with a reduced width at handrails.
paraphrases.R311.7.2: Clear height above the stair must be at least the minimum, measured plumb from the slope line connecting tread edges (or from a landing).
paraphrases.R311.7.3: A single flight may not rise more than the maximum between floors or landings.
paraphrases.R311.7.4: The walkline used for winder measurements runs at a set distance from the inside edge of the stair.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.1|maximum riser: No riser in a flight may be taller than the maximum; riser height is taken plumb from one tread edge to the next.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.1|riser uniformity: In one flight, the tallest riser may exceed the shortest by no more than the allowed variation.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.2|minimum tread: Every tread must be at least the minimum depth, taken level from one tread edge to the next.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.2|tread uniformity: In one flight, the deepest tread may exceed the shallowest by no more than the allowed variation.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.2.1: Winder treads need a minimum depth at the walkline and a minimum depth at the narrow end, with uniformity within the flight.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.3: Tread nosings must project within a set range where risers are closed, and be uniform in a flight, with stated exceptions.
paraphrases.R311.7.5.4: Plastic composite treads on exterior stairs must meet the product standard and labeling requirements.
paraphrases.R311.7.6: A stair needs a landing or floor at its top and its bottom, at least the stair width and of minimum depth, with a stated exception at doors.
paraphrases.R311.7.7: Stair treads and landings may slope no more than a small maximum.
paraphrases.R311.7.8: Flights with more than a set number of risers need a handrail on at least one side, mounted within a set height range above the tread edges.
paraphrases.R311.7.8.3: Handrails must be graspable, with a circular or other profile within stated size limits.
paraphrases.R311.7.8.4: Handrails must run continuously for the full flight, with allowances at newels and turns, and returns at the ends.
paraphrases.R311.7.9: Stair lighting follows R303.7 and R303.8.
paraphrases.R311.7.10: Spiral stairs and basement bulkhead stairs have their own width, tread, riser and headroom rules.
paraphrases.R311.7.11: Alternating tread devices are allowed only in limited locations and must meet stated dimensions.
paraphrases.R311.7.12: Ships ladders are allowed only in limited locations and must meet stated dimensions and handrail rules.
paraphrases.R311.8: Ramps in the egress path may not exceed a maximum slope and need landings of minimum size at top, bottom and turns.
paraphrases.R311.8.3: Ramps steeper than a set slope need handrails on at least one side, meeting the stair handrail rules.
paraphrases.R312.1.1: A guard is needed along an open-sided walking surface, stair or ramp where the drop to the surface below exceeds the trigger height, measured within a horizontal band from the edge.
paraphrases.R312.1.2|general: A required guard must be at least the minimum height, measured from the walking surface.
paraphrases.R312.1.2|Exceptions stairs: Guards along open sides of stairs may be lower, measured from the line through tread edges, and a handrail may serve as the guard within stated heights.
paraphrases.R312.1.3: Openings in a required guard must stop a sphere of the stated diameter from passing, with larger allowances at stair triangles and stair sides.
paraphrases.R312.1.4: Plastic composite guards on exterior walking surfaces must meet the product standard and labeling requirements.
paraphrases.R312.2.1: Operable windows more than a set height above grade with a low sill need fall protection or limited opening; Virginia changes the values (18 in / 72 in).
paraphrases.R312.2.2: Window opening control devices used for fall protection must meet the named standard and not reduce the escape opening below the minimum.
paraphrases.R313.1: Virginia replaces R313 so sprinklers are not required; the design rules apply only where a system is installed (townhouses are outside single-family scope).
paraphrases.R313.2: For the single-family homes in ORI scope, Virginia replaces R313 so a sprinkler system is not required; the design rules apply only where a system is installed.
paraphrases.R314.1: Smoke alarms must be listed to the named standard and installed per their listing.
paraphrases.R314.2: Smoke alarms are required in new construction and in other listed situations.
paraphrases.R314.2.2: The IRC requires smoke alarms when alterations, repairs or additions need a permit; Virginia deletes this section.
paraphrases.R314.3: Smoke alarms are needed in every bedroom, outside each bedroom area, and on every story including basements and habitable attics.
paraphrases.R314.3.1: Smoke alarms must keep stated distances from cooking appliances and bathroom doors, depending on alarm type.
paraphrases.R314.4: Where more than one alarm is required, they must be interconnected so all sound together.
paraphrases.R314.5: Alarms that combine smoke and CO detection may be used if listed to both standards.
paraphrases.R314.6: Smoke alarms need building wiring with battery backup, with stated exceptions; Virginia changes the exceptions.
paraphrases.R314.7: A household fire alarm system may be used instead of single-station alarms if it meets the named standard; Virginia changes this section.
paraphrases.R314.7.3: Virginia rewrites R314.7.3: a household fire alarm system, once installed, becomes a permanent part of the dwelling.
paraphrases.R315.1: Carbon monoxide alarms must be listed and installed per the code and their listing.
paraphrases.R315.1.1: CO alarms must be listed to the named standard; Virginia changes the listing text.
paraphrases.R315.2: Houses with fuel-fired appliances or an attached garage need CO alarms; Virginia changes where they are required.
paraphrases.R315.2.2: The IRC requires CO alarms when permitted alterations are made; Virginia deletes this section.
paraphrases.R315.3: CO alarms go outside each sleeping area near the bedrooms, and inside a bedroom where a fuel-fired appliance is in it or its bathroom.
paraphrases.R315.4: Combination CO and smoke alarms may be used if listed to both standards.
paraphrases.R315.5: Where more than one CO alarm is required, they must be interconnected; Virginia changes this text.
paraphrases.R315.6: The IRC sets the CO alarm power source; Virginia deletes this section.
paraphrases.R315.7: A CO detection system may be used instead of single-station CO alarms if it meets the named standards.
paraphrases.R315.7.3: Virginia rewrites R315.7.3: a household CO detection system, once installed, becomes a permanent part of the occupancy.
paraphrases.R316.1: Foam plastic insulation and trim must follow R316.
paraphrases.R316.2: Foam plastic and its containers must carry labels showing the testing agency and product information.
paraphrases.R316.3: Foam plastic must meet stated flame spread and smoke-developed limits, with a lower limit for roof coverings.
paraphrases.R316.4: Foam plastic inside the house must be covered by a thermal barrier, such as gypsum board of stated thickness, unless an exception applies.
paraphrases.R316.5: The code lists specific uses (attics, crawl spaces, doors, sill plates and others) where foam may use lesser protection.
paraphrases.R316.6: Foam plastic may be used without the normal barrier if approved based on fire tests that represent the installed assembly.
paraphrases.R316.7: In areas of heavy termite risk, foam plastic near the ground must be protected as R318.4 requires.
paraphrases.R316.8: Foam sheathing must resist wind pressures as the code states.
paraphrases.R317.1: Wood in listed locations near the ground, on concrete or exposed to weather must be naturally durable or preservative-treated.
paraphrases.R317.2: Preservative-treated wood must carry the grading or inspection agency's quality mark.
paraphrases.R317.3: Fasteners and connectors in treated wood must be of the stated corrosion-resistant types.
paraphrases.R317.4: Plastic composite decking, treads, guards and handrails must meet the product standard and labeling requirements.
paraphrases.R318.1: In areas subject to termite damage, protection must use one of the listed methods (chemical, bait, barriers or resistant materials).
paraphrases.R318.2: Chemical termiticide treatment must follow the label and include required reapplication after soil disturbance.
paraphrases.R318.3: Physical barriers used for termite protection must be approved and installed to their listing.
paraphrases.R318.4: In very heavy termite areas, foam plastic may not be installed on exterior foundation walls near the ground, with stated exceptions.
paraphrases.R319.1: Buildings need address numbers of minimum size and contrast that can be read from the street.
paraphrases.R320.1: Where accessibility is required (for example by other law), the IBC accessibility provisions apply.
paraphrases.R320.2: Live/work units follow the IBC provisions (outside ORI single-family scope).
paraphrases.R320.3: Virginia adds R320.3: a dwelling not otherwise required to be accessible may follow the USBC universal design section (IBC 1110.17 as amended), and the local building department may approve it as having universal design features.
paraphrases.R321.1: Elevators in dwellings must meet the named elevator safety standard.
paraphrases.R321.2: Platform lifts must meet the named standard.
paraphrases.R321.3: Elevators and lifts in accessible routes must meet the referenced accessibility provisions.
paraphrases.R322.1: Houses in flood hazard areas must be designed to resist flood loads and use the design flood elevation; Virginia changes the lowest-floor and flood-resistant-material subsections (item 35).
paraphrases.R322.2: In A zones, the lowest floor must be at or above the required elevation, with enclosures below it limited and vented; Virginia changes the Coastal A Zone designation and the enclosed garage item (items 35-36).
paraphrases.R322.3: In V zones, houses must be elevated on open foundations with the structure above the required elevation, and spaces below limited; Virginia changes site preparation, enclosed areas and tanks (items 37-38).
paraphrases.R323.1: Storm shelters, where built, must meet the named storm shelter standard.
paraphrases.R324.1: Solar thermal and photovoltaic systems must follow R324 and the referenced codes.
paraphrases.R324.2: Solar thermal systems must be designed and installed to the mechanical and plumbing provisions.
paraphrases.R324.3: PV systems must be listed and labeled to the named standards and installed per the electrical code.
paraphrases.R324.4: Roofs carrying rooftop PV must be designed for the added dead, wind, snow and seismic loads.
paraphrases.R324.5: Building-integrated PV products must meet the roof covering and fire classification requirements.
paraphrases.R324.6: Rooftop PV arrays must leave clear access pathways for firefighters, with stated exceptions.
paraphrases.R324.6.2: PV arrays must stay a set distance below the ridge (Virginia value 18 in).
paraphrases.R324.7: Ground-mounted PV systems must meet the stated structural and clearance rules.
paraphrases.R325.2: Clear height above and below a mezzanine floor must be at least the minimum.
paraphrases.R325.3: A mezzanine may not exceed a set fraction of the area of the room it sits in.
paraphrases.R325.4: Mezzanines need egress meeting the stair, ladder or alternating tread rules.
paraphrases.R325.5: A mezzanine must be open to the room below, with guards where required, subject to exceptions.
paraphrases.R326.2: A habitable attic needs a minimum floor area and clear height over a set share of the area, and must meet the attic definition.
paraphrases.R326.3: A habitable attic is not counted as a story if stated conditions are met; Virginia changes the exceptions.
paraphrases.R326.4: Habitable attics need egress and escape openings as for other habitable spaces.
paraphrases.R327.1: Pools, spas and hot tubs are governed by the ISPSC (the ICC swimming pool and spa code).
paraphrases.R331: Virginia adds R331: a locality in a high radon potential area (EPA Zone 1) that takes official action under state law enforces Appendix AF, with a stated exception.
paraphrases.R332: Virginia adds R332: patio covers follow Appendix AH.
paraphrases.R333: Virginia adds R333: assemblies between dwelling units follow Appendix AK (accessory dwelling units excepted), and envelopes in locally enforced airport noise zones must meet stated sound attenuation.
paraphrases.R334: Virginia adds R334: unless the house has an approved sprinkler system under R313, a kitchen fire extinguisher rated 2-A:10-B:C or approved equivalent is required.
paraphrases.R335: Virginia adds R335: in new dwellings with a kitchen and living area on the egress-door level, one interior route from that door to those rooms (and related spaces) must meet a minimum clear width; not for additions or alterations.
paraphrases.R336: Virginia adds R336: dwellings at or under 400 sq ft may use Appendix AQ as an alternative.
